name: State of Israel

areaKm2.note: Pre-June-1967 armistice lines: official 20,770 km2 (incl. inland water). The world_1960 Israel polygon computes to ~31,100 km2 on the sphere (coarse outline), used as high.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1967 = 2,715k (mid). OWID/HYDE 2,538,658 (low); World Bank 1967 male+female = 2,745,000; high allows for the CBS mid-year figure incl. East Jerusalem after June. Pre-war lines only.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share 1967 = 58.2% (low). Israel CBS national definition (towns of 2,000+) was ~80% in the 1960s, used for high; mid between. Grade C.

activePersonnel.note: Standing force = conscripts + career regulars. CIA/DIA memo 26 May 1967: army average peacetime strength ~55,000; plus air force (~8,000) and navy (~3,000-4,000). COW NMC v7 milper 1967 = 75,000 (high). Mobilised reservists are counted in trainedReserves, not here.

trainedReserves.note: Reservists mobilised by 5 June 1967. CIA/DIA 26 May: 158,000 already mobilised, maximum 280,000 (army) -> up to ~225,000 reservists. Stone 2004 p. 217 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War: total strength incl. reservists 264,000 -> ~193,000 reservists. Reserve brigades formed most of the 1967 ground force.

supportPersonnel.note: Air force, navy, armour and artillery crews, signals, logistics and staff within the ~71,000 standing force. Reconstruction from the CIA army figure plus service strengths; grade C.

mobilizationRatio.note: Achieved: 264,000 under arms (Stone 2004 p. 217 via Six-Day War article) / ~2.7M population = 9.8%; 1973 reached ~12.5%. A total-war ceiling of ~15% is the high.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Standing (conscript/regular) infantry only: Golani, Givati remnants and Nahal line units, ~5-6 battalions-equivalent of 4,000-man brigades (CIA: brigades of ~4,000). Reserve infantry brigades (the bulk) arrive via trainedReserves. Reconstruction, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: FN FAL and Uzi, but many units on mixed WWII-era kit and M3 half-tracks.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75 (professional standing army). Evidence: CIA 26 May 1967 credits high quality of training and operational proficiency.

count.note: Educated guess: paratroop and reconnaissance (Sayeret) conscript units; 55th Paratroop Brigade (reserve) not counted here. Grade C reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: light weapons, limited AT means.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: elite volunteer paratroop and Sayeret units.

count.note: CIA/DIA table: 274 SP antitank/assault guns (M50 155 mm SP, AMX-105, tank destroyers). Towed field artillery estimated ~100-200 more; reconstruction, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: French-built SP guns on Sherman chassis, short-ranged.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: artillery a secondary arm; air force substituted for fire support.

count.note: CIA/DIA table 26 May 1967: Israel 1,123 tanks; text "about 1,000 tanks". Tucker 2004 p. 176 via Six-Day War article: 800. Centurion, M48, upgunned Sherman, AMX-13.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: Centurions with 105 mm L7 among the best, but Shermans and AMX-13 obsolescent.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Tal's gunnery reforms; long-range tank gunnery superiority shown in the 1964-65 water war.

count.note: Educated guess: M3/M5 half-tracks were the IDF APC fleet; no published count fetched. Range brackets the ~1,100 Egyptian APCs in Sinai (Pollack p. 59) which Israel roughly matched.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: WWII half-tracks, open-topped.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: mechanised brigades exercised with armour.

count.note: Split of the CIA/DIA total of 256 operationally assigned jet fighters: ~72 Mirage IIIC plus ~24 Super Mystere B2 in the interceptor role (Oren 2002 / Pollack composition). Grade C for the split.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Mirage IIIC Mach 2 with radar, the IAF best type, comparable to the MiG-21.

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0. Evidence: elite pilots, 7-8 minute turnarounds in Operation Focus; CIA notes high readiness.

count.note: Rest of the 256 jet fighters: Mystere IVA, Ouragan, Vautour II bombers (~160); high includes ~40 armed Fouga Magister trainers used for ground attack. Wikipedia Six-Day War infobox: 250-300 combat aircraft (Oren p. 171, Tucker pp. 540-541).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: subsonic French types of the 1950s.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Operation Focus destroyed ~300 Egyptian aircraft on the ground in hours.

count.note: Educated guess: S-58, Super Frelon, Alouette II/III in IAF service; no fetched count.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: transport helicopters only, no gunships.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: heliborne paratroop raid at Um Katef (Abu Ageila).

count.note: CIA/DIA 26 May 1967: Israel has two destroyers (INS Eilat, INS Yafo; ex-RN Z-class). High allows the old frigate INS Mivtach-era escorts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: WWII-built destroyers; Eilat sunk by Styx missiles in Oct 1967.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: CIA rates Egyptian ships ~80% as effective as Israeli ones.

count.note: Educated guess: Motor torpedo boats and patrol craft; the Sa'ar missile boats were still being built in Cherbourg (Israeli Navy article: missile-boat era begins 1965, delivered 1968-69).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: gun and torpedo craft, no missiles yet.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: small professional navy.

count.note: CIA/DIA 26 May 1967: two submarines (ex-RN S-class Tanin and Rahav).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: WWII-era boats.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: volunteer submarine flotilla since 1959.

count.note: Educated guess: One MIM-23 Hawk battalion (CIA notes "an effective Hawk missile system") of ~4-6 batteries plus 40 mm Bofors AAA batteries around the five airbases.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Hawk was a modern SAM in 1967.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional air force air-defence units.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: single command over interior lines (CIA 26 May 1967); Rabin/Gavish/Tal/Sharon combined-arms plan won in six days.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: reserve brigades with stable territorial membership; strong unit identity.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: existential threat perceived during the May 1967 waiting period; CIA cites the "important, but intangible, morale factor".

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: jet aircraft, 105 mm L7 tank guns, Hawk SAM; no ATGMs or guided air weapons in use.

armor.note: Anchor: 8 = RHA (1943). Evidence: Centurion and M48 cast/rolled steel, no composite armour.

ships.note: Anchor: 8 = radar, submarines. Evidence: WWII destroyers and S-class submarines; missile boats not yet delivered.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8. Evidence: fortified border kibbutzim and bunkers; hardened aircraft revetments (CIA).

logistics.note: Anchor: 8 = motor transport. Evidence: fully motorised supply, rapid reserve mobilisation in 48-72 h (CIA).

communications.note: Anchor: 8 = radio at company level. Evidence: VHF radio nets to tank level, central air control.

isr.note: Anchor: 8 = radar, 9 = satellites. Evidence: excellent HUMINT/SIGINT and photo reconnaissance; no satellites.

air.note: Anchor: air 8 = 1943, 9 = 1985. Evidence: Mach 2 Mirage IIIC with radar and early AAMs; most strike types subsonic.

cyber.note: No military computer-network capability before ~1985 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): Israel 1967 = 9,918 (2011 int$). Range +/-10%.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via OWID: 1966 = 9.4% (last peacetime, low), 1967 = 15.4% (mid, war year), 1968 = 17.4% (high).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry (manufacturing, construction, utilities) about a third of Israeli output in the 1960s; World Bank NV.IND.TOTL.ZS has no Israel value for 1967.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Israel 1967 = 10.9%. Share 10.9% (range 9.0-13.0%) -> 0.891 (0.87-0.91).

annualCohort.note: derived:cohort-from-agegroup with World Bank SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y / FE.5Y and SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN / FE.IN (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ISR;EGY/indicator/SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y?date=1967:1973&format=json). (1,373,628 x 10.80% + 1,371,372 x 10.47%) / 5 = 58,400 persons (men and women; both were conscripted).

artillery.note: Educated guess: Soltam built mortars and some SP conversions on Sherman chassis.

armor.note: Educated guess: no domestic tank production in 1967; only rebuilds and upgunning of Shermans and Centurions.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: IAI licence-built Fouga Magister trainers; no combat-jet production.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess: patrol craft only; missile boats built in France.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: paved roads within the pre-1967 lines (CBS reported roughly 4,000 km in the 1960s).

railKm.note: Educated guess: Israel Railways network ~750 km (Haifa, Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Beersheba lines).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Haifa (main naval base), Ashdod (opened 1965), Eilat (Red Sea, closed by the Tiran blockade in May 1967).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: ZIM-led merchant fleet of the mid-1960s, roughly 0.8-1.1M GRT x 1.5 dwt/grt.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: the IDF reached the Suez Canal ~200-250 km from its Negev bases within four days; CIA 26 May notes regrouping and resupply would be needed before a drive to the canal.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: negligible military role; farm horses and mules only.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS estimate via OWID: Israel 1967 = 2 (improvised devices reportedly assembled during the crisis; never declared). Low 0: not acknowledged, not deliverable by a tested system.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 rows: familiar terrain, fortified border settlements and total population support, but no strategic depth (15 km waist at Netanya).

notes: Snapshot date 5 June 1967 (Operation Focus). Territory and population: pre-war armistice lines, no occupied territories. Personnel convention: activePersonnel = conscripts + career regulars (~71,000); trainedReserves = reservists, already mobilised on 5 June (~190,000-225,000). The P roles hold only standing infantry; reserve infantry and armoured brigades (most of the IDF in battle) enter through trainedReserves. Key sources: CIA/DIA intelligence memorandum "Military Capabilities of Israel and the Arab States", 26 May 1967 (archive.org CIA reading room copy; table: Israel 55,000 prior to mobilisation, 280,000 at M+15, 1,123 tanks, 274 SP AT/assault guns, 256 jet fighters, 2 destroyers, 2 submarines); Six-Day War article infobox (Stone, Oren, Tucker, Pollack citations). IISS Military Balance 1967-68 could not be fetched (paywalled; archive.org copies access-restricted); its Israel entry was not used. Weakest values: half-track count, helicopter and air-defence battery counts (educated guesses).
